title: Functional atlas of vertebrate viral RNA elements that stabilize RNA and enhance translation
title_zh: 脊椎动物病毒RNA元件功能图谱：稳定RNA并增强翻译的元件
abstract: Viruses encode diverse regulatory elements, but their breadth and mechanisms remain poorly defined. To address this gap, we performed massively parallel reporter assays spanning ∼200,000 genomic segments from 297 vertebrate-infecting viral genera. We identified numerous viral elements that enhance RNA stability and translation through TENT4-mediated mixed tailing, distributed across 19 genera and grouped into six distinct subclasses, indicating extensive convergent evolution. We also found diverse TENT4-independent elements acting through alternative pathways. One such element, Pt1 from Potamipivirus, stabilizes linear mRNA to levels comparable to circular RNA, suggesting its potential for RNA therapeutics. Pt1 directly recruits canonical poly(A) polymerases (PAPγ/α)-previously thought to function exclusively in transcription-coupled nuclear pre-mRNA processing-to drive cytoplasmic polyadenylation. Together, these findings chart the rich landscape of viral regulation, extend the scope of poly(A)-tail biology, and establish the virome as a valuable source for uncovering host RNA regulatory mechanisms.
abstract_zh: 病毒编码了多样的调控元件，但其范围与作用机制仍未被充分界定。为填补这一空白，我们对297个感染脊椎动物的病毒属中的约200,000个基因组片段进行了高通量平行报告基因测序实验。我们鉴定出许多通过TENT4介导的混合加尾（mixed tailing）增强RNA稳定性和翻译的病毒元件，这些元件分布于19个属，并可归为六个不同亚类，表明存在广泛的趋同进化。我们还发现了多样化的TENT4非依赖性元件，且其通过替代通路发挥作用。来自Potamipivirus的Pt1就是其中一个例子，它可使线性mRNA的稳定性提升到与环状RNA相当的水平，提示其在RNA治疗中的潜在应用价值。Pt1可直接招募经典聚腺苷酸聚合酶（PAPγ/α）——这些酶此前被认为仅参与转录偶联的核内前mRNA加工——从而驱动细胞质中的多腺苷酸化。总体而言，这些发现描绘了病毒调控的丰富景观，拓展了poly(A)尾生物学的研究范围，并将病毒组学确立为挖掘宿主RNA调控机制的重要资源。
